t:
The Federal Reserve Act is amended by inserting immediately after section 9 the following new section:


“section 9A. participation in lotteries prohibited

“(a) A State member bank may not—

“(1) 
deal in lottery tickets;


“(2) 
deal in bets used as a means or substitute for participation in a lottery;


“(3) 
announce, advertise, or publicize the existence of any lottery;


“(4) 
announce, advertise, or publicize the existence or identity of any participant or winner, as such, in a lottery.



“(b) A State member bank may not permit—

“(1) 
the use of any part of any of its banking offices by any person for any purpose forbidden to the bank under subsection (a), or


“(2) 
direct access by the public from any of its banking offices to any premises used by any person for any purpose forbidden to the bank under subsection (a).



“(c) As used in this section—

“(1) 
The term ‘deal in’ includes making, taking, buying, selling, redeeming, or collecting.


“(2) 
The term ‘lottery’ includes any arrangement whereby three or more persons (the ‘participants’) advance money or credit to another in exchange for the possibility or expectation that one or more but not all of the participants (the ‘winners’) will receive by reason of their advances more than the amounts they have advanced, the identity of the winners being determined by any means which includes—

“(A) 
a random selection;


“(B) 
a game, race, or contest; or


“(C) 
any record or tabulation of the result of one or more events in which any participant has no interest except for its bearing upon the possibility that he may become a winner.



“(3) 
The term ‘lottery ticket’ includes any right, privilege, or possibility (and any ticket, receipt, record, or other evidence of any such right, privilege, or possibility) of becoming a winner in a lottery.




“(d) 
Nothing contained in this section prohibits a State member bank from accepting deposits or cashing or otherwise handling checks or other negotiable instruments, or performing other lawful banking services for a State operating a lottery, or for an officer or employee of that State who is charged with the administration of the lottery.


“(e) 
The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System shall issue such regulations as may be necessary to the strict enforcement of this section and the prevention of evasions thereof.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the word "participation" in the heading triggers a Yes, but that only refers to banks taking part in lotteries, and the substantive prohibitions involve no outside-party process. The section nonetheless qualifies because subsection (e) requires the Board of Governors to issue regulations, and a rulemaking mandate counts as participation under the definition.
fable.s: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System shall issue such regulations as may be necessary to the strict enforcement of this section and the prevention of evasions thereof.

qwen_block.w: The section primarily prohibits State member banks from participating in lotteries. The word 'participation' appears only in the title and in the definition of a lottery (referring to lottery participants, not public participation in government decisions). The only procedural requirement is for the Federal Reserve Board to issue regulations, which is an internal executive action. There is no requirement for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards involving non-federal members before the decision to issue regulations or enforce the ban.
qwen_block.s: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System shall issue such regulations as may be necessary to the strict enforcement of this section and the prevention of evasions thereof.

opus.w: Subsection (e) requires the Federal Reserve Board to issue regulations, and the definition counts required rulemaking as participation because it brings in public notice and comment. The word "participation" elsewhere in the section is a red herring: it describes people playing lotteries, not outsiders taking part in a federal decision. The label rests only on the rulemaking mandate.
opus.s: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System shall issue such regulations as may be necessary to the strict enforcement of this section and the prevention of evasions thereof.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** One tempting reading is to say "Yes" because the word "participation" appears in the heading and the lottery definitions. That reasoning is wrong: those uses refer to people taking part in lotteries, not to anyone taking part in a federal decision. The opposite temptation is to say "No" because the section is only a ban on banks. That fails too. Subsection (e) requires the Board of Governors to issue regulations, and under the definition, required rulemaking counts as participation. The answer is "Yes" because of subsection (e), not because of the keyword.

qwen_chat.w: This section prohibits state member banks from dealing in lottery tickets or advertising lotteries. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision. The term 'participation' refers to individuals buying lottery tickets, not to public participation in government decision-making. The requirement for the Board of Governors to issue regulations is an internal agency function, not a form of public participation.
qwen_chat.s:
“section 9A. participation in lotteries prohibited

“(a) A State member bank may not—

“(1) 
deal in lottery tickets;
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The section title is "participation in lotteries prohibited," and the text defines "participants" in a lottery. One might mistakenly think this involves public participation in a government decision because of the word "participation." However, this is a prohibition on commercial activity (dealing in lottery tickets) by banks, not a procedural requirement for the government to consult with outsiders. The "participants" mentioned are people buying lottery tickets, not people advising the government. The only procedural element is the Board of Governors issuing regulations, which is an internal agency action, not a consultation with outsiders.
